Steep slope areas possessing a 30 percent and above slope gradient characterize visually distinctive hill and ridge features. The majority of these areas line valleys and small steep-sided canyons formed by major creeks and drainages, such as Sarpy Creek, East Fork of Sarpy Creek, Pleasant Creek and Spring Creek. Tract II contains a significantly greater amount of land having greater than 30 percent slopes than Tract III. In addition to their destinctive terrain features, many of the steep slope areas are characterized by exposed red, pink or white colored soils and a low density of vegetation cover.
Numerous sandstone outcrops are present within Tracts II and III.

These geologic formations occur both along the sides and tops of steep ridges and on the flat valley floors and upper plateaus. The sandstone outcrops are predominantly yellow to tan in color and often create visually striking formations which contrast with the surrounding vegetation, soils and topography.
Vegetative cover constitutes a primary portion of the perceived landscape in this area, forming a variety of textures, patterns and colors. The plant communities within Tracts II and III which contribute to the overall scenic character include riparian communities, ponderosa pine, grasslands and shrubs, and agriculture.
